images.caption:
Finishing works on Grafton Bridge in Auckland City, New Zealand, ca 1910. Looking northwest towards the modern-day Auckland CBD. 
Extended information on origin webpage reads: Grafton Bridge, Auckland, under construction [ca 1910] / Reference number: 1/2-000889-G 1 b&w original negative(s). Dry plate glass negative 4.5 x 6.5 inches. Horizontal image. / Part of  Price, William Archer, d 1948 :Collection of post card negatives (PAColl-3057) Photographic Archive / Scope and contents: View of Grafton Bridge, Auckland, under construction, circa 1910 taken from the Park Road end. Graves can be seen in Symonds Street Cemetery on the lefthand side in the gully below the bridge. Houses can be seen on the righthand side (St Martin's Street and Symonds Street). Men are working on the roadway, some on steam rollers, and pedestrians are walking across the bridge while it is still under construction. A horse and carriage is in the immediate foreground. Photograph taken by William Price.

images.filename: Grafton Bridge From Eastern Abutment I.jpg
images.caption: Grafton Bridge in Auckland City, New Zealand. Seen from the northern side of the eastern abutment, looking west. The bridge as of the time of the photo had just been through a major maintenance and seismic / load-capability upgrading. While that nicely respected the heritage values, the new cable duct along the pedestrian railing doesn't. Ah, well, few people will ever notice it.

images.filename: Grafton Bridge, Signals For The Clueless.jpg
images.caption: Grafton Bridge in Auckland, New Zealand. Looking west from the intersection with Grafton Road. Notice the overhead lane signals installed after hundreds claimed to not have seen the "bus lane" signs and got dinged with fines. I can understand non-locals to be a bit confused and then miss the signs, but others really had much less excuse. Still, we got this as a result, probably cost only a few hundred grand ;-).
images.alt: Grafton Bridge in Auckland, New Zealand. Looking west from the intersection with Grafton Road.
